display.purpose: Hero headlines and singular page-level statements. One per screen maximum. Instrument Serif only.

headline.purpose: Section headings, feature titles, marketing sub-headlines. Instrument Serif only.

title.purpose: Card headers, sidebar section labels, table section titles. Inter 600 only.

body.purpose: All descriptive prose. Maximum 65ch on marketing surfaces, 72ch in documentation. Inter 400 only.

label.purpose: Navigation section dividers, table column headers, eyebrow tags. Uppercase, Inter 600 only.

shadows.name: sh-sm
shadows.purpose: Default card lift. Structural, not decorative. The minimum elevation above the Warm Cream ground.

shadows.name: sh-md
shadows.purpose: Hover state for interactive cards and focused panels. Signals responsiveness.

shadows.name: sh-lg
shadows.purpose: Marketing illustrations and decorative browser-window mockups. Not used in the product app.

shadows.name: sh-xl
shadows.purpose: Modal overlays, hero login card, maximum elevation for floating panels.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for all UI state transitions. Fast-in, graceful-out.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions: hover color shifts, badge state changes, focus ring appearance.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Standard UI feedback: button hover lift, input focus glow, nav item activation.

motion.name: duration-expand
motion.purpose: Reveal transitions: accordion expand, panel slide-in, modal entry.

narrative.overview:
Eascess is a product that sells trust. Its customers are enterprise IT managers and compliance officers who must be convinced that a third-party script is safe enough to inject into a production website. The visual language earns that trust the same way a well-prepared audit report does: precision, consistency, and calm. Nothing is decorative. Nothing performs. The Warm Cream surfaces give the system human warmth; the Instrument Serif display type carries authority; the Inter body copy stays highly legible under any ambient light.

The system uses a restrained color strategy. The tinted cream surface dominates approximately 90% of every screen. Instrument Teal and Dusk Navy appear only at the edges: the primary CTA, the brand mark, active navigation states, and semantic status signals. Their scarcity is the point.

This system explicitly rejects: consumer-startup playfulness, cold government flatness, and dark-mode-first aesthetics. It also rejects the SaaS dashboard reflex of identical metric-card grids and big-number hero sections.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream surfaces as the universal ground — never stark white, never grey
Instrument Serif at display and headline scale only; Inter everywhere else
A single gradient accent reserved for the brand mark and primary CTA
Shadows appear only on state change, never as ambient decoration
Animations under 200ms, exponential ease-out only; suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion
WCAG 2.2 AAA contrast as a non-negotiable baseline

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The brand gradient (Instrument Teal to Dusk Navy at 135 degrees) fires exactly twice per screen: the primary CTA button and the brand mark. It does not appear as a decorative background wash, a card accent, or a text fill. Its rarity is what makes it signal authority instead of noise.

rules.name: The Parchment Test
rules.body: If any surface reads as stark white at arm's length, it is wrong. Every background must use the Warm Cream scale. Pure white is reserved only for card surfaces that sit visibly raised atop the cream page ground.

rules.name: The Quiet Serif Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif appears only at Display and Headline scale. It is never set at body or label size. A small-size Instrument Serif is a misconfigured template, not a design choice.

rules.name: The Italic Authority Rule
rules.body: Italic Instrument Serif appears only for emphasis within a Display or Headline span, never as a stylistic default. It carries specific semantic weight and should occur at most once per headline.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. sh-sm is the minimum structural card lift; sh-md through sh-xl are earned through interaction or overlay context. A design that assigns sh-lg to a static widget is using shadow as decoration, which is prohibited.

dos: Do set every background to the Warm Cream scale. Pure white is reserved only for card surfaces floating above the cream ground.
Do reserve Instrument Serif exclusively for Display and Headline scale.
Do use italic Instrument Serif to mark a key phrase within a headline span, at most once per headline.
Do treat the brand gradient as a once-per-screen signal: primary CTA button and brand mark only.
Do suppress all transitions and animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do pass WCAG 2.2 AAA contrast on every new color pairing before shipping.
Do write explicit label elements for every form input.
Do include :focus-visible styles on every interactive element.
Do keep UI feedback transitions under 200ms with ease-out-quart.
Do animate only transform and opacity.
donts: Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient fill. Gradient text is prohibited.
Don't use a border-left or border-right wider than 1px as a colored accent stripe on any card, list item, or navigation element.
Don't use emoji as icons in primary UI surfaces.
Don't place the brand gradient on large background areas or section washes.
Don't use neon colors, rainbow gradients, or high-chroma fills outside the defined semantic tokens.
Don't produce a cold, clinically white layout. Every background must pass the Parchment Test.
Don't use dark mode as the primary theme.
Don't apply box-shadow to static surfaces that don't change elevation state.
Don't use the hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stat row, gradient accent.
